analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md (head lines 1059-1072): it adds a documentation paragraph and bash block for SDK 27.2 Date-comparison and weak-import checks (scripts/test-check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/test-check-provider-weak-imports.py, scripts/check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py). It touches no runtime code, keys, attestation, WebSocket contract, cache storage (T-041), add-on hold socket (TB-012/T-059/T-060), installer (TB-013/T-061), or authorization (TB-011/T-053/T-054). The text says the checks run without a Mac against recorded nm/otool output from a crashed DevNet build and that the release lane runs the weak-import check on built binaries. This introduces no new attack surface and weakens no mitigation. I also read the surrounding base text (add-on hold, App Attest dispatch, native qualification, cluster and release tests) as unchanged context. It consistently disclaims physical qualification, and I found no overclaim of security properties. Unverified contract: whether the referenced scripts exist and are wired into Release Integrity is outside the supplied evidence, since only the docs change is visible. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. No findings.
